description: Bootstrap: project is scaffolded, dependencies installed, dev server and backend are running, and all required static assets are in place
steps: Verify frontend/ directory exists with src/, public/tiles/, and contracts/ subdirectories
Run npm install inside frontend/ and confirm it exits 0 with all required packages present (maplibre-gl, deck.gl, react-hook-form, zustand, ajv, msw)
Run tsc --noEmit inside frontend/ and confirm it exits 0 with no type errors
Start the Vite dev server and confirm it serves the app at localhost:5173 without errors
Confirm the FastAPI backend is running and GET /api/schema/scenario returns HTTP 200
Verify frontend/public/tiles/tiles.pmtiles exists on disk

description: JSON Schema contract files committed to repo as single source of truth
steps: Verify /contracts/entity.schema.json exists in the repository
Verify /contracts/scenario.schema.json exists in the repository
Confirm both files use JSON Schema draft-07 with x- extension properties
Validate that no field definitions are duplicated in frontend or backend code
Confirm ajv 8 (frontend) and NJsonSchema (C# backend) both resolve against these files

description: API contract file defines all endpoint signatures, request/response shapes, and binary slice wire format
steps: Verify /contracts/api.md exists in the repository
Check that all REST endpoints are listed with their HTTP method and path
Confirm request and response shapes are documented for each endpoint
Verify HTTP status codes are documented for each endpoint
Confirm the binary slice wire format (56-byte header + Float32Array) is fully specified

description: Map functions with no internet connection (air-gapped/offline support)
steps: Disconnect the machine from the internet
Open the application in a browser
Verify the map renders vector tiles without any network requests to external CDNs
Confirm tile requests are served from frontend/public/ via Vite static middleware
Verify the PMTiles file (tiles/tiles.pmtiles) is present under frontend/public/

description: Application opens with an interactive map centered on a default location
steps: Navigate to the application root URL
Verify the map renders on page load without errors
Confirm the map is centered on the configured default location
Check that the map is interactive (zoom, pan) immediately on load
Verify no spinner or loading state blocks map interaction

description: Scenario panel is displayed in a left sidebar alongside the map
steps: Open the application
Verify a left sidebar panel is visible
Confirm the map fills the remaining right portion of the viewport
Scroll or interact with the scenario panel and verify the map remains visible
Check that the sidebar is full height

description: Scenario form fields are rendered from the JSON Schema served by the backend at runtime
steps: Open the application and wait for the schema to load from GET /api/schema/scenario
Verify form fields for name, height range, height step, angular resolution, grid cell size, terrain toggle, and combination method are rendered
Add a new field to the schema on the backend and reload the app
Confirm the new field appears in the form without a frontend rebuild
Verify no scenario field definitions are hardcoded in frontend source code

description: User can add between 2 and 10 entities to a scenario
steps: Open the application and navigate to the scenario panel
Add a first entity and verify it appears in the entity list
Add a second entity and verify the scenario allows submission
Continue adding entities up to 10 and verify all are accepted
Attempt to add an 11th entity and verify the UI prevents it

description: Entity form fields are rendered from the entity JSON Schema served by the backend
steps: Open the application and wait for schema to load from GET /api/schema/entity
Add an entity and verify fields for label, position, frequency, power, azimuth, antenna height, and radius are rendered
Add a new field to entity.schema.json on the backend and reload the app
Confirm the new field appears in the entity form without a frontend rebuild
Verify no entity field definitions are hardcoded in frontend source code

description: User can place an entity by clicking on the map
steps: Open the application and add an entity
Click a point on the map
Verify a marker appears at the clicked location
Confirm the entity's lat/lon fields in the form update to match the clicked coordinates
Click a different map location and verify the marker and form fields update accordingly

description: User can drag an entity marker to update its position
steps: Open the application and place an entity marker on the map
Click and drag the marker to a new location
Verify the marker moves smoothly while dragging
Release the marker and confirm it stays at the new position
Verify the entity's lat/lon form fields update to the new coordinates after the drag

description: Lat/lon coordinate fields stay in bidirectional sync with the map marker
steps: Place an entity marker on the map and note the lat/lon form values
Manually type new coordinates into the lat field and verify the map marker moves
Manually type new coordinates into the lon field and verify the map marker moves
Drag the marker to a new position and verify the lat/lon form fields update
Confirm neither input method causes an infinite update loop

description: Each entity's radius is visualized as a filled circle on the map
steps: Add an entity with a non-zero radius value
Verify a filled circle is rendered on the map centered on the entity marker
Add a second entity and verify it also shows its own radius circle
Verify circle radii are correctly scaled to match the entity's radius field value
Confirm circles are rendered as a GeoJSON fill layer

description: Radius circle updates in real time as the radius field value changes
steps: Place an entity on the map with an initial radius value
Change the radius field value to a larger number
Verify the circle on the map immediately grows without page reload
Change the radius field value to a smaller number
Verify the circle on the map immediately shrinks

description: Numeric fields display a unit suffix indicating the expected unit
steps: Open an entity form and locate the frequency field
Verify 'MHz' is displayed as a suffix next to the frequency input
Verify 'dBm' is displayed next to the power field
Verify 'm' or 'km' is displayed next to applicable distance fields
Confirm unit suffixes are display-only and not included in the submitted form value

description: Fields with x-show-if conditions hide or show dynamically based on other field values
steps: Open the scenario form and locate a field with an x-show-if condition
Set the controlling field value to the condition's trigger value
Verify the conditional field becomes visible
Change the controlling field value to a non-triggering value
Verify the conditional field is hidden

description: numeric-or-file fields allow toggling between an inline value and a file path
steps: Open an entity form and locate a numeric-or-file field (e.g. frequency or power)
Verify the field defaults to inline numeric input mode
Click the toggle to switch to file path mode
Verify a file path input is displayed in place of the numeric input
Toggle back to numeric mode and verify the numeric input is restored

description: Form validation runs on blur and on submit, enforcing type checks and min/max constraints
steps: Enter an invalid value (e.g. text in a numeric field) and tab away
Verify a validation error appears immediately on blur without submitting
Clear the error by entering a valid value and verify the error disappears
Submit the form with one or more invalid fields
Verify all invalid fields show errors and submission is blocked

description: Clear inline error messages appear next to each invalid field
steps: Submit the scenario form with empty required fields
Verify an error message is displayed directly adjacent to each invalid field
Confirm error messages describe the specific constraint violated (e.g. 'Required', 'Must be >= 0')
Fix one invalid field and verify its error message disappears while others remain
Fix all fields and verify all error messages clear on successful submission

description: Submitting a scenario shows a job progress indicator immediately
steps: Fill out a valid scenario form
Click the submit button
Verify a job progress indicator appears immediately after submission
Confirm the indicator is visible while the job is running
Verify the scenario_id and job_id from the POST response are stored and used

description: Job progress streams in real time via SSE without polling
steps: Submit a scenario and observe the network tab
Verify an EventSource connection opens to /api/scenarios/{scenario_id}/jobs/{job_id}/events
Confirm progress messages from the SSE stream update the UI in real time
Verify no polling requests (repeated GET/POST calls) are made during job execution
Confirm the EventSource connection closes when a done or error event is received

description: Heatmap overlay appears automatically when the job completes
steps: Submit a scenario and wait for the SSE done event
Verify the heatmap overlay renders on the map automatically without user action
Confirm the heatmap is positioned correctly over the map
Verify the default height slice is fetched and rendered immediately on job completion
Check that the heatmap layer is visible and not blocked by other UI elements

description: Height slider allows scrubbing through height levels of propagation output
steps: Complete a scenario run so the heatmap is displayed
Locate the height slider at the bottom of the map
Drag the slider to a different height level
Verify the heatmap updates to show the propagation data for the selected height
Scrub through multiple levels and confirm each level loads and renders correctly

description: User can type a specific height value numerically in addition to using the slider
steps: Display the heatmap after a completed run
Locate the numeric input adjacent to the height slider
Type a specific height value into the numeric input
Verify the slider moves to the corresponding position
Confirm the heatmap updates to reflect the typed height value

description: Adjacent height levels (±2) are prefetched in the background for smooth scrubbing
steps: Complete a scenario run and observe the network tab
Select a height level on the slider
Verify fetch requests for the two levels above and two levels below the current selection are made in the background
Scrub to an adjacent level and verify it renders immediately without a loading delay
Confirm the ring buffer holds at most 5 slots and evicts old entries when full

description: Heatmap is rendered as a GPU-accelerated R32F texture via a custom Deck.gl layer
steps: Complete a scenario run and wait for the heatmap to appear
Verify the heatmap layer is implemented as a custom Deck.gl layer
Confirm the Float32Array from SliceParser is uploaded as an R32F WebGL texture
Verify the GLSL color ramp is applied (min → black, max → yellow)
Check that the heatmap renders at interactive frame rates on a large grid

description: Null cells outside entity radius areas render as transparent on the heatmap
steps: Complete a scenario run with entities covering only part of the map area
View the heatmap overlay on the map
Verify cells outside all entity radius areas are fully transparent
Confirm the NaN value check in the GLSL shader discards those fragments
Verify the underlying map tiles remain visible through the transparent cells

description: Heatmap is positioned correctly on the map using bounding box from the slice header
steps: Complete a scenario run and display the heatmap
Verify the heatmap bounds (west, south, east, north) are read from the 56-byte slice header
Confirm the heatmap overlay is geographically aligned with the map
Pan and zoom the map and verify the heatmap moves correctly with the map
Check alignment against known entity positions to confirm correct georeferencing

description: User can save a completed run by giving it a name
steps: Complete a scenario run so the heatmap is displayed
Click the save run action
Enter a name for the run in the save dialog
Confirm the save action POSTs to the save endpoint with the provided name
Verify the run is stored and the saved state is reflected in the UI

description: Confirmation dialog appears before an unsaved run is deleted
steps: Complete a scenario run without saving it
Trigger a re-run or action that would overwrite the current unsaved run
Verify a confirmation dialog appears with 'Save & Re-run', 'Discard & Re-run', and 'Cancel' options
Click 'Cancel' and verify no data is lost and the dialog closes
Click 'Discard & Re-run' and verify the unsaved run is deleted and a new run starts

description: User can re-run a scenario after modifying parameters
steps: Complete an initial scenario run
Modify one or more scenario parameters in the form
Click the re-run action
Verify the modified parameters are submitted in the new POST request
Confirm the new run's heatmap replaces the previous one after completion

description: evaluateShowIf is a pure function with no side effects, unit testable without DOM or form context
steps: Locate the evaluateShowIf function in the codebase
Verify it accepts a condition object and a form values object as arguments
Confirm it returns a boolean with no side effects
Run unit tests covering and/or operators, all six ops (eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte), missing fields, and nested objects
Verify tests pass without any DOM, React, or form framework imports

description: SliceParser is a pure function that parses an ArrayBuffer and returns a typed result
steps: Locate the SliceParser function in the codebase
Verify it accepts a raw ArrayBuffer and returns { width, height, minVal, maxVal, bounds, data: Float32Array }
Run unit tests with a valid ArrayBuffer fixture and verify the parsed result is correct
Run unit tests with wrong magic bytes and verify a typed SliceParseError is thrown
Run unit tests with a truncated buffer and a zero-size grid and verify errors are thrown correctly

description: SchemaFormRenderer accepts a schema object and react-hook-form control as props, testable in isolation
steps: Locate the SchemaFormRenderer component in the codebase
Verify it accepts schema, control, and watch as props with no hardcoded field names
Render SchemaFormRenderer in a test with a fixture schema and a test form control
Assert the correct field renderers are mounted for each property in the fixture schema
Verify x-show-if conditions hide and show fields correctly within the isolated test

description: Zustand stores are instantiated via factory functions so each test gets a fresh store
steps: Locate the Zustand store definitions for mapStore, jobStore, and uiStore
Verify each store is created via a factory function rather than a module-level singleton
Write a test that creates two store instances via the factory
Mutate state in the first instance and verify the second instance is unaffected
Confirm no global state leaks between test runs when using the factory pattern

description: Integration tests cover the full flow: form fill → validation → POST → SSE → heatmap render
steps: Locate the integration test suite for the golden path flow
Verify MSW is used to mock the HTTP layer (schema fetch, POST, SSE, slice fetch)
Fill the scenario form with valid data in the test and submit
Simulate SSE progress events and then the done event via the MSW handler
Assert the heatmap Deck.gl layer receives the correct Float32Array and bounds from SliceParser
